title: SQL Set 06: Logistics, Warehousing & Inventory Thresholds
description: Stockout detection, carrier SLA compliance, cross-warehouse stock comparison, and cumulative weight packing.

queries.title: SKUs Below Reorder Point Across All Warehouses
queries.prompt: Find `sku` and `total_qty` for products whose summed `qty_on_hand` across all `stock` rows is strictly less than their `reorder_level` in `sku_master`. Order by `sku`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE sku_master (sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY, reorder_level INT); CREATE TABLE stock (wh_id INT, sku TEXT, qty_on_hand INT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO sku_master VALUES ('SKU-A',50),('SKU-B',30),('SKU-C',20); INSERT INTO stock VALUES (1,'SKU-A',20),(2,'SKU-A',25),(1,'SKU-B',35),(2,'SKU-C',10),(3,'SKU-C',10);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT m.sku, COALESCE(SUM(s.qty_on_hand), 0) AS total_qty FROM sku_master m LEFT JOIN stock s ON m.sku = s.sku GROUP BY m.sku, m.reorder_level HAVING COALESCE(SUM(s.qty_on_hand), 0) < m.reorder_level ORDER BY m.sku;
queries.explanation: `LEFT JOIN` ensures even zero-stock SKUs would appear; `SKU-C` has 20 which is not strictly `< 20`.

queries.title: Carrier On-Time Delivery Rate
queries.prompt: Compute `carrier` and `on_time_pct` (percentage of parcels where `delivered_date <= promised_date`, rounded to 1 decimal place), keeping only carriers with at least 2 parcels. Order by `on_time_pct` DESC, `carrier` ASC.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE parcels (parcel_id INT PRIMARY KEY, carrier TEXT, promised_date TEXT, delivered_date TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT carrier, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_date <= promised_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS on_time_pct FROM parcels GROUP BY carrier HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY on_time_pct DESC, carrier ASC;
queries.explanation: ISO-8601 date strings (`YYYY-MM-DD`) compare chronologically; `HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2` excludes single-parcel carrier `Xpress`.

queries.title: Select Boxes Within Truck 1000kg Capacity
queries.prompt: Boxes in `cargo` are loaded in ascending `load_order`. Return `box_id` and `weight_kg` of boxes that fit before cumulative weight exceeds 1000 kg. Order by `load_order`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE cargo (box_id INT PRIMARY KEY, load_order INT, weight_kg INT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH cum AS (SELECT box_id, load_order, weight_kg, SUM(weight_kg) OVER (ORDER BY load_order) AS running_wt FROM cargo) SELECT box_id, weight_kg FROM cum WHERE running_wt <= 1000 ORDER BY load_order;
queries.explanation: Running sum hits `350 + 400 + 250 = 1000` at box 30; box 40 reaches 1150 and is excluded.

queries.title: Distinct City Route Pairs with Both-Way Flights
queries.prompt: From `routes (origin, dest)`, find pairs `(city_a, city_b)` with `city_a < city_b` such that BOTH `(city_a -> city_b)` and `(city_b -> city_a)` exist. Order by `city_a`, `city_b`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE routes (origin TEXT, dest TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT r1.origin AS city_a, r1.dest AS city_b FROM routes r1 JOIN routes r2 ON r1.origin = r2.dest AND r1.dest = r2.origin WHERE r1.origin < r1.dest ORDER BY city_a, city_b;
queries.explanation: The `r1.origin < r1.dest` predicate eliminates reversed duplicate pairs like `(DEL, BLR)` alongside `(BLR, DEL)`.

queries.title: Express Tracking Numbers Matching Regional Prefix
queries.prompt: Return `tracking_no` and `hub` from `dispatch` where `tracking_no` starts with `'IND-'` and ends with `'-EXP'`, sorted alphabetically by `tracking_no`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE dispatch (tracking_no TEXT PRIMARY KEY, hub TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT tracking_no, hub FROM dispatch WHERE tracking_no LIKE 'IND-%-EXP' ORDER BY tracking_no;
